text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Monday.

LONDON - Britain's leading share index fell for the third straight session but ended off the day's lowest level after Wall Street recovered from an early sell-off. The FTSE 100 closed at 4895.7, down 3.6 points, or 0.07 percent.

FRANKFURT - German shares generally declined in floor trading as the DAX index fell 2.69 percent on interest rate concerns and pessimism left over from late electronic trading on Friday. The DAX-30 index closed at 4296.94, down 111.85 points, or 2.54 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 4302.50, down 34.48 points, or 0.80 percent.
PARIS - French shares slumped nearly 2 percent on concerns that interest rates were headed higher, brokers said. The CAC-40 index closed at 2992.41, down 57.03 points, or 1.87 percent.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed sharply lower, loosing more than 2 percent in the blue-chip SMI index as fears of rising interest rates in the United States and possibly Germany put pressure on prices, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5,771.0, down 127.2 points, or 2.16 percent.

TOKYO - The Tokyo stock market's key index closed moderately lower, paring its losses after briefly dipping below the key support point of 19,500. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 19,668.07, down 136.31 points, or 0.69 percent.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong share prices took a tumble with the banking sector leading the way as investors sold down HSBC Holdings Plc shares ahead of the banking giant's interim results. The Hang Seng index closed at 16,259.59, down 119.63 points, or 0.73 percent.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market ended 0.8 percent lower in reaction to U.S. weakness, but turnover was meagre as a bank holiday in New South Wales sidelined many investors. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,706.0, down 21.5 points, or 0.79 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended near the day's weakest levels as a soft opening on Wall Street knocked already sliding stocks, distressed by the rand's fall to fresh six-month lows on the U.S. dollar, down further. The all-share index closed at 7,445.2, down 11.6 points, or 0.16 percent. The all-gold index closed at 970.1, up 6.3 points, or 0.65 percent, while the industrial index closed at 9,110.2, down 35.3 points, or 0.39 percent.
